column1: # ZAP baseline triage. TAB separated: rule id, action (WARN|IGNORE|FAIL), reason.
# Everything not listed here defaults to WARN and appears in the artifact. A
# rule is moved to FAIL only once somebody has read a real report and decided
# the finding is real for this API -- a gate that fails on its first run is a
# gate somebody deletes, and then nothing is scanned at all.
# Every IGNORE below has a reason, and the reason is checkable.

column3: Incidental caching headers. This is a JSON API behind bearer auth; no page is cached by a shared cache, and the CSP/HSTS work that matters lives on the web app (docs/security/CSP.md).
X-Content-Type-Options is set by helmet on the API and by middleware on the web app. ZAP reports it against error responses emitted before helmet runs.
Information disclosure via suspicious comments. Hits on the RFC 9457 problem-detail bodies, which name the failing route on purpose.
Server header. Express is fingerprintable regardless; hiding it is theatre and the version is not published.
Permissions-Policy is a document header. The API serves JSON, not documents.
Cross-domain misconfiguration. The CORS allow-list is explicit and asserted in s14-csrf.exploit.spec.ts; ZAP reads a wildcard preflight it did not send credentials on.
